name: Zadok
overview: Zadok is a male Levite identified as the son of Meraioth, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:11. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with a note suggesting he may be a duplicate of another Zadok (Zadok_3). There is limited information about his personal role or actions beyond his lineage within the tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Zadok means 'righteous one' and is a proper name found in Nehemiah 11:11. This meaning reflects a characteristic often associated with individuals in biblical narratives, though the name was not given directly by God in this instance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zadok as the son of Meraioth explicitly and infers that Meshullam is his father. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zadok's significance lies chiefly in his genealogical placement among the Levites, indicating his role within the priestly or Levitical lineage during the post-exilic period. The brief mention in Nehemiah 11:11 situates him among those who returned to Jerusalem, emphasizing continuity of Levitical heritage. The note about a possible duplicate highlights the challenges of identifying individuals with common names in Scripture but does not diminish his part in the biblical record.
